The quadratic factor ${x}^{2}+1$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\frac{2}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+1)}=\frac{A}{x-1}+\frac{Bx+C}{{x}^{2}+1}.
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x-1)({x}^{2}+1),$ and we get

$$
2=A({x}^{2}+1)+(Bx+C)(x-1).
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=1,B=-1,$ and $C=-1.$ Therefore,

$$
\frac{2}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+1)}=\frac{1}{x-1}+\frac{-x-1}{{x}^{2}+1}.
$$

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{x-1}+\frac{-x-1}{{x}^{2}+1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we have

$$
\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $u={x}^{2}+1.$ Then $\text{d}u=2x\,\text{d}x,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+1| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we use the fact that $\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{a}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{a}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{a}),$ which results in

$$
\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡x.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{(x-1)({x}^{2}+1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)-\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+K\end{aligned}
$$
